content: Zidovudine can reduce the number of certain white blood cells, leading to anemia and muscle disorders. When used alone or with other antiviral drugs, it may cause severe liver damage and a condition called lactic acidosis. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms such as nausea, loss of appetite, dark yellow or brown urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, flu-like symptoms, yellowing of the skin or eyes, pain in the upper right abdomen, muscle weakness, lack of strength, muscle pain, shortness of breath, extreme fatigue, or pale skin. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and undergo laboratory tests to monitor your response to zidovudine. Zidovudine is prescribed to treat HIV infection, either alone or in combination with other medications, in patients with or without AIDS. It works by slowing the spread of HIV in the body. However, it is not a cure for HIV and may not reduce the occurrence of HIV-related illnesses. Zidovudine does not prevent the transmission of HIV to others, except when administered to HIV-positive pregnant women to reduce the risk of passing the infection to their baby. Despite this treatment, there is still a possibility of HIV transmission to the infant. Zidovudine is available as capsules, tablets, and syrup, and is typically taken three to four times daily, though in some cases it may be taken five times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take zidovudine exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Zidovudine is sometimes used to treat healthcare workers or others exposed to HIV through accidental contact with contaminated blood, tissues, or bodily fluids. Discuss the potential risks of this treatment with your doctor. Before starting zidovudine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially acetaminophen, acyclovir, aspirin, cimetidine, fluconazole, foscarnet, ganciclovir, indomethacin, interferon, lorazepam, oxazepam, probenecid, valproic acid, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have had liver or kidney disease, muscle disorders, anemia, a history of alcohol abuse, or any blood-related conditions. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking zidovudine, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, let your doctor know if you consume alcohol. Zidovudine should be taken at least 30 minutes before or one hour after a meal. Take it while sitting upright and with plenty of water. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Common side effects of zidovudine include stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation, headache, dizziness, and difficulty sleeping. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. If you develop a rash or any of the severe symptoms mentioned earlier, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store zidovudine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or stops breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Zidovudine is sold under brand names such as Retrovir® (including Retrovir® IV Infusion and Retrovir® Syrup). It is also available in combination products like Combivir® (with lamivudine) and Trizivir® (with abacavir sulfate and lamivudine). Other names for zidovudine include AZT and ZDV.
